lesson: Small paste scale (0.3-0.7) is the dominant lever: best mAP50 (0.604) and best patches AP50 (0.79), confirming the small-miss hypothesis. Balanced allocation beat inclusion-heavy, and any_class backgrounds badly hurt inclusion (0.21) — keep same_class + balanced + small scale. Next round: build on small scale and probe whether going even smaller (0.3-0.5) or prefer_small sources recovers the still-missed smallest instances, while keeping same_class pool.

candidates.hypothesis: Misses concentrate in the small size tertile for every class, so shrinking paste scale to 0.3-0.7 (covering the 25-60px missed range) should raise small-instance recall and mAP. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 jumps well above 0.18 and low-tertile recall improves vs control; if flat, scale is not the lever.

Inclusion's low AP50 (0.18) may be data scarcity (10 real images) rather than scale. Doubling its allocation (25/12/13) at the default scale should lift inclusion AP without hurting the other classes. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 rises more than in candidate 1/control while patches/scratches hold.

Scratches have the highest FP rate (0.22/img) and low-contrast instances are missed everywhere; pasting onto any_class backgrounds adds texture diversity and co-occurring defects, improving precision/robustness. Confirmed if precision (esp. scratches) improves vs control without recall loss.
CONTROL (added by the lab): default generation recipe, balanced allocation.

lesson: Inclusion-heavy allocation (24/13/13) at small scale 0.3-0.7 gave the best mAP (0.625) and best worst-class AP (0.3845) with inclusion recall up to 0.363 — inclusion is data-limited, so keep feeding it. Scratch mid-scale 0.5-1.0 was clearly worse (mAP 0.593, scratch AP did not recover), refuting 'small pastes hurt scratches' — keep scratches at 0.3-0.7. The control (repeat R1) swung wildly (patches 0.79->0.71, inclusion 0.35->0.41) at mAP 0.591, so per-class deltas under ~0.05 are noise; in the final round build on inclusion-heavy + 0.3-0.7 and avoid untested extreme allocations.

candidates.hypothesis: Inclusion misses center on ~34px instances, smaller than the 0.3-0.7 pastes produced in R1 (which left inclusion AP flat at 0.355). Shrinking inclusion pastes to 0.3-0.5 (~27-45px from ~90px sources) should match the missed size band and lift inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 with improved low-tertile recall; if inclusion AP drops instead, 0.3-0.7 was already the sweet spot and scale is not the inclusion lever.

Inclusion is data-starved (10 real images, AP 0.355, recall 0.25) and R1's inclusion-heavy test was confounded by using default scale. Shifting budget to inclusion (24/13/13) while keeping the proven 0.3-0.7 small scale should raise inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 without dropping patches/scratches by more than ~0.03; if inclusion stays ~0.35, allocation is not the lever and the problem is purely scale/appearance.

Scratch AP fell 0.714->0.667 when pastes shrank to 0.3-0.7 (beyond the ~0.03 noise band), suggesting very small thin-line pastes are unlearnable noise, yet missed scratches (median 41.8px) are small. A mid scale 0.5-1.0 (~36-73px from ~73px sources) should recover scratch AP50 toward ~0.71 while keeping patches/inclusion at their proven 0.3-0.7; if scratches do not recover, the R1 drop was noise and per-class scale tuning is unnecessary.

lesson: Inclusion scale 0.3-0.5 + heavy allocation (24/13/13) is the proven sweet spot: best inclusion AP (0.41) and best worst-class AP, confirming missed inclusions are a scale problem, not a source-identity problem (appearance-matched sources did not help). prefer_small source weighting is harmful for thin-line scratches (AP -0.06) — keep uniform weighting there. If iterating further, the only untested inclusion lever left is going even smaller (0.3-0.4) or raising max_overlap; do not touch scratch/patch scale.

candidates.hypothesis: Missed inclusions (median 34px, 146/179 in low tertile) are small vertical dark streaks/blobs; the large irregular source 99 is a poor match. Restricting inclusion pastes to the 8 small/vertical sources (11, 150, 50, 268, 277, 100, 106, 131) at the proven 0.3-0.7 scale should lift inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 and mAP above 0.625; if inclusion AP stays ~0.38, appearance-matched source selection is not the lever.

R2 tested 0.3-0.5 with balanced allocation (0.6205) and 0.3-0.7 with heavy allocation (0.625) separately; the missing cell is 0.3-0.5 + heavy. Since missed inclusions center at ~34px (0.3-0.5 of ~90px sources = 27-45px), tightening the inclusion scale band while keeping the proven 24/13/13 allocation should raise inclusion AP50 toward 0.40+; if it merely ties the control, 0.3-0.7 was already the sweet spot and scale is not the remaining inclusion lever.

Missed patches (49px vs 85px train median) and scratches (40px vs 73px) are also systematically smaller than what uniform-source pastes produce, so biasing both classes toward smaller sources (prefer_small) at the proven 0.3-0.7 scale should improve their low-tertile recall and lift patches/scratches AP50 above 0.785/0.705 without touching the proven inclusion recipe; if either class drops by >0.03, small-source bias is harmful and uniform weighting stays.
